To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the data on the partial photoneutron cross sections of 188,189Osmust be corrected for systematic errors associated with the experimental neutron multiplicity counting and that the cross section of total photoneutron (γ, xn) reaction can be reliably evaluated by means of an experimental-theoretical analysis.
the cross sections of the partial photoneutron reaction, (γ, in) on 188, 189Os isotopes are determined with a high degree of reliability and accuracy.

the cross sections of the partial photoneutron reaction on 188, 189Os isotopes are evaluated using an experimental-theoretical analysis of data obtained in experiments using quasimonomode annihilation γ-beams and neutron multiplicity sort method.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a reliable determination of the cross sections of photoneutron reactions for 188, 189Os isotopes, free of neutron multiplicities sorting problems, which is a necessary condition for a reliable determination of nuclear level densities.
the reliable experimental cross sections of the partial photoneutron reaction on 188, 189Os isotopes.
the development of a reliable method to determine cross sections of partial neutron photoreactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experimental cross sections for partial photoneutron reaction on 188, 189Os isotopes obtained using neutron multiplicity sorting methods are not reliable.
the experimental data on the cross section of partial photoneutrons reactions on 188Os and 189Os isotopes are unreliable.

the cross sections of the partial reactions on 188Os and 189Os isotopes, obtained in the experiment using neutron multiplicity sorting, contain significant systematic errors and cannot be used in the analysis of the experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cross sections of the partial photoneutron reaction on 188, 189Os isotopes, evaluated within the framework of the experimental-theoretical approach, are reliable and can be used for the construction of a new set of photonuclear data for the Os isotopes in the energy range from threshold up to 20 MeV.
the cross section of partial photoneutrons reactions (γ, in) for 188Os and 189Os isotopes are obtained for the first time with the accuracy of about 10%.
the experimental data obtained for 188Os and 189Os isotopes with the use of neutron multiplicity counting are in a poor agreement with the data obtained by the method proposed in [1].
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cross sections of photoneutron partial reactions, which are free of neutron multipicity sorting problems, can be obtained by the experimental-theoretical approach, which uses a quasimono-energetic photon beam and an appropriate choice of the experimental conditions.

the experimental cross sections obtained by the neutron multiplicity sorting technique can contain significant systematic errors, and therefore the data on partial photoneutron reaction cross sections should be evaluated with caution.
, when analyzing the cross sections of the partial photoneutron reaction, it is necessary to take into account the experimental errors in the cross sections of total photoneutron reactions.
